scope: P9 P2P independent microphone/screen-audio sinks and guarded capture controls
behavior: Two independent playPrivateAudio leases consume remoteMicrophoneStream and remoteScreenAudioStream; remoteStream remains video-only and is never an audio fallback.

Each playback lease checks the exact source stream, live raw audio track set, call object and participant IDs, peer connection, account owner/generation and selected output device. Weak ownership bindings prevent retained streams or raw tracks from being relabelled across sources, calls, connections or logins.

Microphone volume uses masterVolume times userVolumes; shared audio uses masterVolume times screenShareVolumes. Local deafen and per-peer local mute gate both. Guild server-deafen is intentionally excluded from private-call playback. Source failure/retry, revocation and output changes retire only the correct owners.

Explicit system-audio choice reads screenAudioRequested and calls setScreenAudioRequested only for the current active account/call/connection with advertised peer support, before screen sharing and outside isScreenSharePending. No UI invocation starts a second picker or implies later audio auto-enablement.

The UI displays actual off/starting/shared/not_returned/unavailable/ended states. Starting/shared expose the render-captured stopScreenAudio action; controls also validate captured call object, peer connection, account owner/generation and current action reference before invoking it. The source-bound store action remains responsible for the exact media ticket.

Personal volume and checkbox handlers reject stale render callbacks after account, generation, connection or call replacement. Pending picker/restore is visibly disabled and stale checkbox handlers also recheck live pending state.

Windows consent explicitly describes system audio from all other applications excluding HiChat; browser consent describes audio only when returned by the selected-source picker. Existing group consent/status translations are reused. Real en/tr i18next rendering verifies the voice namespace, separate personal volumes and source-state labels.
